research_question: Does a repository-local estimate of Generator Task yield per Git touch, applied to current Git pressure, predict the next generated Task-module mix better than full Task history and either component alone?

candidate.name: Generator-Calibrated Module Exposure
candidate.mechanism_hypothesis: On the explicitly projected source timeline, a fixed Generator and admission policy induce a stable module-specific association between eligible Git change exposure and generated Task mass.
candidate.historical_task_mass: one unit per admitted historical Task split uniformly across its retrospective eligible reference-patch modules
candidate.historical_exposure: one unit per reachable non-root non-merge commit split uniformly across eligible touched modules, from the repository's first selected source Task time through the Origin cutoff
candidate.recent_exposure: the identical commit-touch exposure with a fixed exponential age kernel
candidate.git_walk_policy: walk the complete reachable non-merge DAG with git rev-list --since-as-filter so an old-timestamp ancestor cannot hide a deeper in-window commit; apply the observation-start and cutoff filters again after projection
candidate.prior: fixed empirical Task-per-touch rate shrinkage with repository-global mean and exactly one-half Task of regularization mass
candidate.statistical_interpretation: The dimensional form is motivated by Gamma-Poisson rate shrinkage, but fractional multi-module Task and commit mass are not literal Poisson counts and q_m is not claimed as an exact conjugate posterior.
candidate.projected_timeline_boundary: Task time is the source created_at projection while Git exposure uses commit time; reference-patch attributes may mature later. The study tests a projected-timeline association, not a native event-time causal thinning process.
candidate.positive_task_zero_exposure_rule: retain the fixed finite shrinkage estimate and report Task mass on modules with zero observed historical Git exposure; do not hard-fail or silently drop such modules
candidate.no_recent_exposure_rule: G_m=0 contributes exactly zero candidate mass; no epsilon or additive recent-exposure smoothing
candidate.zero_total_rule: a repository-Origin with zero historical or recent eligible exposure is a data admission failure, not a fallback forecast

module_projection.path_rule: first two parent-directory components; use the available prefix when shorter
module_projection.path_input_rule: Git --name-only paths are already repository-relative and retain real top-level a/ or b/ directories; reference-patch diff headers remove exactly one side prefix before applying path_rule
module_projection.git_path_transport: read git show --name-only with NUL delimiters so whitespace, non-ASCII names, and Git quotePath behavior cannot alter module identity
module_projection.task_label_rule: unique eligible paths in the source reference fix patch, split uniformly; no eligible path maps to OTHER
module_projection.origin_vocabulary: ROOT, OTHER, cutoff-safe historical Task modules, and reachable eligible Git modules
module_projection.future_unseen_rule: a future patch module absent from the Origin vocabulary maps to OTHER

rolling_origin.remainder_policy: leading remainder is absorbed into the initial history so every retained future cohort is a complete non-overlapping H10 block
rolling_origin.block_policy: H5 is the first five Tasks in the same H10 block
rolling_origin.ordering: declared source Task time then canonical Task identity
rolling_origin.task_time_projection: every timezone-naive SWE-rebench V2 created_at value is explicitly assumed UTC for counterfactual development
rolling_origin.origin_snapshot: latest first-parent commit on the frozen default-branch history whose committer time is at or before the Origin cutoff
rolling_origin.future_dated_ancestor_policy: clamp structurally reachable negative clock age to zero and report the count

source.frame_rule: canonical repositories whose pinned source aliases contain at least 75 rows before exact canonical-PR deduplication; include all passing repositories, with no top-N choice or replacement
source.canonical_task_identity: when meta.pr_url is present and its case-insensitive owner/repository agrees with either the source alias or resolved canonical repository, canonical repository plus decimal PR number; otherwise the source instance_id
source.duplicate_rule: canonical duplicates must agree on base commit, created_at, language, and patch; retain complete source-ID lineage and one canonical Task
source.base_commit_policy: record exact per-Task Git commit-object presence as a diagnostic lineage digest; absence does not reject a Task because this counterfactual Task-mix study uses source time plus reference-patch modules and never checks out a Task base
source.head_policy: head_ref records freeze-time provenance; head_commit is the authoritative replay object and later live movement of the named branch does not invalidate the frozen study

metrics.primary: future Task-module multiclass Brier score with fractional mass for multi-module Tasks
metrics.reason: The fixed mechanism permits structural zero recent exposure; Brier is a proper score that does not require an outcome-chosen epsilon.
metrics.descriptive: total variation and Origin-to-final-Task calendar span
metrics.aggregation: Tasks to Origin, Origins to canonical repository, repositories equally

decision_gate.complete_source_admission: all 40 canonical repositories produce complete H5/H10 evidence; no failed repository is replaced or silently removed
decision_gate.row_integrity: derive each repository's exact numbered Origin set from expected_task_count and rolling_origin; reject unknown repositories, missing or extra Origins within every observed repository, horizons outside H5/H10, duplicate repository-Origin-horizon rows, and any Origin missing its paired H5 or H10 row before aggregation
decision_gate.h5: candidate minus full Task history, git_recent_touch, and yield_only are each negative with repository-bootstrap upper bounds below zero; the full-history contrast also has at least 24/40 favorable repositories
decision_gate.h10: the identical three bootstrap contrasts and 24/40 full-history favorable condition hold
decision_gate.pass: both H5 and H10 gates pass
decision_gate.failure: retire THY-002 without changing prior shape, half-life, module map, frame threshold, repository membership, timestamp policy, metric, horizon, or gate

outcome_boundary.agent_results: prohibited in this study even if Task-mix gates pass
outcome_boundary.claim: A pass supports only generator-conditional counterfactual Task-mix prediction on a new automated Generator family. It would require a separately frozen Selection and Agent-outcome study.

result_verification: require exact study identity, plan digest, zero-valued paid/embedding/Agent-outcome/sealed-holdout counters, source and repository manifest digests plus plan identities, a complete admitted-or-failed repository partition, unique complete Origin rows, replayed repository summaries, and replayed decision
forbidden_post_replay_changes: searching another prior strength, half-life, exposure window, module depth, exclusion list, Task-count threshold, repository subset, metric, or horizon
dropping repositories, Origins, OTHER, zero-yield modules, or future Tasks after patch projection
using future patches, future Task counts, Agent outcomes, or source metadata enrichment as candidate inputs
promoting origin-weighted, language-subgroup, calendar-subgroup, or total-variation results after the repository-first Brier gate fails
